resources.title: Three things every home runs on
resources.intro: Electricity, water and what you throw away. You pay for all three and see almost none of it. Groundwork puts a number on each.

energy.name: Energy
energy.body: The most the central government pays towards a home rooftop solar system under PM Surya Ghar. Groundwork works out what your roof and your bill would qualify for.

water.name: Water
water.body: What a toilet that keeps running can waste. Two readings, one at night and one before anyone wakes up, are enough to catch it.

waste.name: Waste
waste.body: Since April 2026, homes separate waste into wet, dry, sanitary and special care. Photograph a pile and Groundwork sorts it, and tells you what your dry waste is worth to a recycler.

free.a: Yes. Groundwork is free for households. We don't sell your number or your bill to installers.

safe.a: We read only the numbers we need: units, amounts, the billing period and your sanctioned load. We don't keep your consumer number or address, and the photo itself is deleted within 7 days. You can download or delete everything from Settings at any time.

where.q: Which states and DISCOMs does it cover?
where.a: Groundwork has the full residential tariff for {list}, each transcribed from the regulator's order. For any other DISCOM we use the average rate from your own bill, and we tell you the result is less precise.

accurate.a: Tariffs come from the regulator's order and the subsidy from the government's own rules. Sunlight comes from NASA's 20-year records for your exact location. Our yearly generation estimate was within {pct}% of the European Commission's PVGIS model in all five cities we checked. Installer quotes vary, so you can replace our cost estimate with a real quote.

installers.a: No. Groundwork doesn't install anything or take a cut from your bill. The report is yours to take to any installer, and it links to the official PM Surya Ghar portal for the subsidy.

howItWorksPage.metaDescription: How Groundwork reads your bill, meter and waste, does the maths in code, and tracks what you actually save.
howItWorksPage.title: How Groundwork works
howItWorksPage.intro: Groundwork turns the phone you already have into a meter for electricity, water and waste. AI reads the photos. Ordinary, tested code does every calculation. You see the working for every number.
howItWorksPage.principle1Body: AI models read your photos and explain results. Every number you see comes from a tested formula, never from a model's guess.
howItWorksPage.principle2Body: After we read a bill, you see each field with how sure we are about it, and you can correct anything before the maths runs.
howItWorksPage.principle3Body: A solar plan is a projection until you install it. Your ledger keeps what could happen apart from what did.
howItWorksPage.energyBody: Photograph the bill. We read the units, the period, your sanctioned load and the amount, and you check them. Then we recalculate your bill from your DISCOM's tariff, size a rooftop system to your use, your roof and your load, apply the PM Surya Ghar subsidy, and work out the payback month by month at your own slab rates.
howItWorksPage.waterBody: Log a reading late at night and again early in the morning, before anyone uses water. If the meter or tank moved overnight, something is leaking. Groundwork estimates the litres lost per day and walks you through finding it. Litres saved count only after you fix it and use actually drops.
howItWorksPage.wasteBody: Photograph a pile and Groundwork names each item, its stream under the 2026 rules, and how to dispose of it. Weigh roughly, see an indicative scrap value, and request a pickup from a recycler listed near you.
howItWorksPage.alsoNote: Ask the copilot about any of it, in English, Hindi or Marathi. Bring your housing society along to see your combined savings.

methodologyPage.metaDescription: Every formula, constant and tariff Groundwork uses, with its source and date.
methodologyPage.title: Methodology
methodologyPage.intro: Every number Groundwork shows comes from a formula on this page, using a constant or tariff listed here with its source. This page is generated from the same files the calculations read, so it can't drift from the maths.
methodologyPage.solarIntro: How we size a system and work out its cost, savings and payback. Each step below is a step in the report's "How we calculated this" drawer.
methodologyPage.constantsIntro: Values marked as our assumption are shown as such in every report, and the ones that vary most (cost and price rise) can be changed on the report.
methodologyPage.tariffsIntro: Residential tariffs transcribed from each regulator's order. Charges that change month to month, like the fuel adjustment charge, are taken from your own bill.
methodologyPage.fixedPerConnection: ₹{single} a month (single phase), ₹{three} a month (three phase)
methodologyPage.fixedByUnits: ₹{tiers} a month, depending on units used; ₹{three} a month for three phase
methodologyPage.fixedPerKw: ₹{rate} per kW of sanctioned load per month
methodologyPage.fixedByBand: Per kW of sanctioned load per month: {bands}
methodologyPage.extraAboveKw: Plus ₹{inr} per {block} kW (or part) above {above} kW
methodologyPage.pvgisIntro: We compare our yearly output for 1 kW with PVGIS, the European Commission's solar model, in five cities. Our model assumes flat panels, so it reads lower than PVGIS at its best tilt, especially in the north. That keeps estimates on the cautious side.

aboutPage.metaDescription: Why Groundwork exists and how it is built.
aboutPage.title: About Groundwork
aboutPage.p1: Most Indian homes pay for electricity, water and waste disposal without seeing what they actually use. Bills arrive as a total. Leaks run silently in overhead tanks. Recyclables with real value go to landfill.
aboutPage.p2: Groundwork measures before it advises. It starts from your own bill, your own roof and your own meter, puts a rupee figure on each fix, and keeps score of what actually changed.
aboutPage.p3: It is built on AWS, with AI models reading photos and plain, tested code doing every calculation. It is independent: no DISCOM, installer or scheme pays for what we say.
aboutPage.nameNote: Not to be confused with the Groundwork environmental charities in the UK and USA. We're an Indian product for Indian homes.
aboutPage.contactBody: Questions, corrections to a tariff or a fact on this site, or a society that wants to try Groundwork: write to <email>{address}</email>.

privacyPage.metaDescription: What Groundwork stores, why, and how to delete it.
privacyPage.title: Privacy
privacyPage.summary: We store the numbers we need to give you advice, not your documents. Bill photos are deleted within 7 days. You can download or delete everything at any time.
privacyPage.store1: Your account: your email address and name, through Amazon Cognito.
privacyPage.store2: Your home: city, a map pin for your roof, roof area, household size, DISCOM and water source, as you enter them.
privacyPage.store3: Numbers from your bills and readings: units, amounts, billing periods, sanctioned load, meter readings, and waste weights and categories.
privacyPage.notStore1: Your consumer number or address from a bill. We don't read them.
privacyPage.notStore2: Bill, meter and waste photos beyond 7 days. They are deleted automatically.
privacyPage.notStore3: Payment details. Groundwork doesn't take payments.
privacyPage.aiBody: Photos you upload, and questions you ask the copilot, are sent to Google's Gemini models to read the numbers and write answers. Google may use these inputs to improve its services, and its reviewers may see them, so cover names and account numbers before you upload. Text read from a photo is treated as data only. Uploaded photos are deleted after 7 days.
privacyPage.shareBody: Only you. If you join a housing society, other members see only combined totals, and your flat appears on the leaderboard only if you opt in. If you request a waste pickup, the recycler you choose gets the items, their rough weights, your preferred date, your note and your email address, so they can reach you. We don't sell your data or share it with installers or anyone else.
privacyPage.controlBody: From Settings you can download all your data as JSON or CSV, delete single entries, or delete your account, which removes your profile, every record and every file.
privacyPage.whereBody: On AWS in the Mumbai region (ap-south-1), encrypted at rest.
privacyPage.store5: If you run a recycling business and apply to be listed: your business name, area, city, phone number, the materials you buy, and your email if you give one.

termsPage.title: Terms of use
termsPage.p1: Groundwork's figures are estimates based on your inputs, published tariffs, public data and the assumptions shown on every report. They are not a quote, a guarantee of savings, or financial advice. Check with a registered installer and your DISCOM before you buy.
termsPage.p2: Subsidy and tariff rules are set by the government and regulators and can change. Eligibility for PM Surya Ghar is decided on the official portal, not by Groundwork.
termsPage.p3: Keep your sign-in details private. Upload only bills and photos you are entitled to share. You can close your account at any time from Settings.
termsPage.p4: Don't misuse the service, try to access other people's data, or overload it. We may limit the number of AI scans per hour to keep Groundwork free.
termsPage.p5: We may update these terms. If a change matters, we'll tell you in the app before it applies.

hunt.title: Find the leak
hunt.intro: Work through these. Most household leaks are one of the first three.
hunt.toilet: Toilet: put a few drops of food colouring in the cistern. If colour appears in the bowl within 15 minutes without flushing, the flapper is leaking.
hunt.float: Tank float valve: if water trickles from the overflow pipe, the float valve isn't shutting.
hunt.taps: Taps and showers: look for drips and wet marks under basins.
hunt.pipes: Hidden pipes: damp patches on walls or ceilings mean a pipe leak. Call a plumber.
hunt.fixedDone: Marked fixed on {date}. We'll count the litres saved once your use drops.
hunt.notYet: We'll count savings once a few days of readings show your use has dropped.
hunt.noDrop: Your use hasn't dropped yet. The leak may still be running.

societyPage.title: Society
societyPage.intro: Bring your housing society together. Members see combined totals for the society; nobody sees your own bills, readings or logs.

create.title: Start a society
create.body: You'll be the admin. You get an invite code to share in your society's group.
create.name: Society name

join.title: Join with an invite code
join.body: Ask your society admin for the code.
join.notFound: That code doesn't match a society. Check it with your admin.

you.title: How you appear
you.flatHint: For example A-302. Shown only on the leaderboard, and only if you opt in.
you.nicknameHint: Used on the leaderboard instead of your flat, if you set one.
you.optInHint: Your name or flat and your change against your own past use. Nothing else.

errors.name: Enter the society's name.
errors.flats: Enter the number of flats, from 2 to 5,000.
errors.already: You're already in a society. Leave it first.

invite.title: Invite neighbours
invite.body: Share this code or link. Anyone with it can join.

stats.leaksFixed: {count, plural, =0 {none fixed yet} one {# fixed} other {# fixed}}
stats.none: Nothing realised yet. Totals appear as members log savings, readings and waste.
stats.smallNote: Totals combine every member's ledger. In a society with only a few members, others may be able to work out yours.

board.title: Leaderboard
board.body: Ranked by change in electricity use against each home's own past bills. Lower is better.
board.hidden: {count, plural, one {# household isn't} other {# households aren't}} shown because they haven't opted in.

ann.title: Announcements
ann.placeholder: Write an announcement for every member

leave.confirm: Leave {name}? Your own data stays in your account.
leave.adminNote: As admin, leaving hands the admin role to the longest-standing member.

report.title: Society impact report
report.projectedTitle: What members' plans would add each year
report.leaks: {found, plural, =0 {No leaks found} one {# leak found} other {# leaks found}}, {fixed} fixed
report.method: Totals are the sum of every member's own ledger entries, recalculated when this report is made. Projections and realised savings are kept apart. Households appear by name only if they opted in.

solar.title: Solar for common areas
solar.intro: Panels on the terrace can run the lifts, pumps and common lights. Societies get their own PM Surya Ghar subsidy: ₹18,000 per kW, up to 3 kW per home.
solar.perHome: Shared across {homes} homes: about {cost} each, saving {savings} a year each.
solar.tariffNote: Common-area meters are billed on the residential tariff ({tariff}). Estimates use the regulator's published rates.
solar.notFeasible: The terrace is too small for a 1 kW system.
solar.unitsHint: The average from recent bills for the common meter.
solar.loadHint: Printed on the common meter's bill.
solar.already: Solar residents already got a subsidy for (kW)
solar.alreadyHint: Optional. It counts toward the society's limit.
solar.costHint: Optional. Without one we use a typical price.

errors.load: Enter the sanctioned load in kW.
errors.units: Enter the units used in a month.
errors.terrace: Enter the terrace area in square feet.
errors.already: Enter kW, or leave it blank.
errors.cost: Enter the quote in rupees, or leave it blank.
errors.location: Add your home's location first, so we can look up sunlight.
errors.generic: We couldn't work that out. Try again.

reportsPage.title: Reports
reportsPage.impactCardBody: Everything your home has saved, how each number was worked out, and every source. Save it as a PDF to share.
reportsPage.cardsBody: Each bill compared with the bills before it, per day of use. Grades are against your own past, never other homes.
reportsPage.cardsEmpty: Add two bills with billing dates to get your first report card.
reportsPage.solarRow: {kw} kW · saves about {inr} in year one
reportsPage.notFeasible: Not enough roof for a useful system

impact.title: Impact report
impact.printHint: Your browser's print dialog has a “Save as PDF” option.
impact.realisedBody: Measured numbers come from your readings and bills. Estimated numbers are worked out from what you did, like an installed solar system's expected output.
impact.projectedBody: Projections from your latest reports. They are not savings until they happen.
impact.workingTitle: How each number was worked out

activity.bills: {count, plural, =0 {No bills} one {# bill} other {# bills}} added
activity.solarReports: {count, plural, =0 {No solar reports} one {# solar report} other {# solar reports}}
activity.installed: Solar system of {kw} kW installed on {date}
activity.leaks: {found, plural, =0 {No leaks found} one {# leak found} other {# leaks found}}, {fixed} fixed
activity.waste: {count, plural, =0 {No waste logged} one {# waste log} other {# waste logs}}: {kg} kg, of which {diverted} kg kept out of landfill

impact.method: Groundwork does every calculation in code. AI only reads photos and words tips; it never produces a number in this report. Each total is the sum of individual ledger entries, recalculated when the report is made. Projections and realised savings are kept apart.

copilotPage.title: Copilot
copilotPage.intro: Ask about your electricity, water or waste. Answers use your own data, and every number comes from Groundwork's calculations.
copilotPage.placeholder: Ask about your bills, water or waste
copilotPage.uploadFailed: That photo didn't upload. Try again.
copilotPage.rateLimited: You've asked a lot in the last hour. Try again in a little while.
copilotPage.aiNote: AI can misread photos. Check readings before you save them.

cards.notFeasible: Your roof doesn't have room for a useful system.
cards.leakBody: About {litres} litres a day, found on {date}.
cards.openWaste: Log it on the Waste page
